exposure: Surgery indication (primary CS vs. urgent CS)
cohort: 11,932 patients who underwent cesarean section and were included in the QUIPS pain registry between 2010 and 2020
finding: Severe pain after cesarean section is prevalent and significantly impacts daily activities and recovery, with modifiable factors such as distraction, relaxation, and patient-controlled analgesia showing protective effects.
mod_finding: While pain severity was similar between primary and urgent CS, women who underwent urgent CS received more analgesics and experienced greater impairment in ambulation and deep breathing.
